note: Re-adjudication of the eight v1 AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE_REGISTER cases under Stage-Q v2 rule C (judge from reader-facing framing only; a visible 'Scenario:' label is not automatically sufficient; hidden provenance neither rescues nor condemns). v1 labeled ALL EIGHT as DEFECT/MATERIAL. These re-adjudications are owner-approved development labels for the diagnostic set; they are NOT the v2 qualification gate (that uses fresh holdout cases). Reasonable adjudicators may differ on the INCONCLUSIVE cases; that is itself evidence the v1 labels were not stable.
panelV1Reading: all three judges ruled CLEAN on all eight (reader-facing scenario label + generic names = adequately constructed)

cases.title: Sarah Marks the Blank Page Before the Review
cases.reason: Two named individuals (Sarah, Mathieu) + exact tenures ('eighteen months', 'trusted for fourteen years') + exact time (7:35 a.m.) + specific setting narrated in present tense. The 'Scenario:' label alone does not clearly mark this heavy documentary texture as hypothetical (rule C: 'Scenario' by itself is not automatically sufficient). RETAINS a defect verdict.
cases.changeFromV1: retained (DEFECT), but reclassified as reader-facing framing inadequacy, not provenance-metadata mismatch

cases.title: Claire Closes the Roadmap Spreadsheet
cases.reason: Two names (Claire, Jonas) + specific time/props, but opens with a reflective question and lacks tenure anchoring. Genuinely borderline: a reader might or might not take it as a specific real incident.

cases.title: Grace Deletes the First Defense
cases.reason: Two names (Grace, Miriam) + exact time (8:42 p.m.), but generic chat/transcript props and a clearly illustrative decision beat. Borderline.

cases.title: Hannah Marks Her Own Arrow
cases.reason: Single generic first name, no second person, no exact time/tenure, generic tools (dashboard, Slack). Past-tense illustrative teaching vignette under a Scenario label — a reasonable reader would not take it as a documented real event.

cases.title: Rachel Writes the Real Meeting
cases.reason: Single generic name, generic office props (campaign board, budget email), no anchoring specifics. Illustrative vignette.

cases.title: Laura Opens the Review Notes
cases.reason: Opens 'What if the red cell is not a formatting issue?' — an explicit hypothetical marker framing the whole vignette. Rule C: explicit hypothetical framing is normally adequate.
cases.changeFromV1: FLIP: DEFECT → CLEAN (strongest — explicit hypothetical marker)

cases.title: Anna Separates Repair from Apology
cases.reason: Single generic name, generic release-process props, no time/tenure/real-entity anchor. Illustrative vignette.

cases.title: Emily Rewrites the Co-Parent Opener
cases.reason: Opens in second person ('You see the child's rain boots...'), addressing the reader as a hypothetical actor before naming Emily. The second-person instructional frame is visibly hypothetical.

summary.interpretation: The v1 labels were NOT stable: 7 of 8 change under the corrected reader-facing standard. The panel's uniform CLEAN reading matches v2 on 5, is defensible on 2, and diverges only on the single heaviest case (SQ-017) — confirming STAGE_Q_INSTRUMENT_INVALID rather than judge incapacity.
summary.disposition: All 8 move to the v2 DEVELOPMENT/diagnostic set; NONE gate v2 qualification. Fresh source-register holdout cases (deterministic, complete-evidence) qualify the panel.
